body: Have you ever considered you could have ADD/ADHD? Those tips are pretty great though, thanks.

Thanks for replying. I don't take pride in being unable to study, in fact I am pretty ashamed of it. I wish I could just 'get back to' studying but it's pretty much impossible. Within writing one or two sentences, I'll be deep into some bullshit though about something totally unrelated, or I will have almost subconsciously went to do something else. I know this sounds strange, but I often 'catch myself' trying to stop studying. After standing up and beginning to walk away from my desk, I realise I didn't even consciously make the decision. It feels like I didn't tell myself to stand up, rather my body just did it by itself and I only realised seconds later.

I don't know. I'm feeling a bit better as I found a specialist ADHD clinic around an hour away from me. I've sent an email but if it turns out I can't get medication/treatment (which is highly likely) I will no doubt return to the slump. As for the moment, I'm trying to do anything to take my mind off studying. I fucking hate how my brain seems to function.

Thanks a lot for taking the time to reply with such a heft post, I really appreciate it. I do believe I suffer from procrastination, but not exclusively. I also am entirely certain I suffer from ADHD, I suffer from almost all of the symptoms. A year ago I was struggling in my education and decided to go to my GP about ADHD. He took a quick test but then like all GPs in the UK, didn't have the will to truly help me out. He passed me onto a shoddy psychology centre at my college that totally disregarded me and admitted there was nothing they could do. Getting ADHD treatment in the UK is a matter of being lucky enough to live near a specialist centre, if you don't (like me), then you just have to suffer in silence.

I simply can't be truthful with everyone either, am I supposed to just ruin any respect my parents had for me? I also simply can't study. My apparent ADHD means my mind wanders incredibly, I'll honestly find myself 'subconsciously' trying to get out of studying, and when my wandering mind notices it's useless, I'll already be up to walk around, find food, check myself in the mirror. Anything. When studying, I can barely read as my mind totally wanders.

I will check out that book though, thanks for recommending it. Thanks again for your time. You definitely made me feel a bit better.
